consent.title: Instagram Use Study
consent.ethics: Ethical approval: this study is awaiting review by the University of Surrey's ethics committee. Its approval reference will be shown here once approval is granted.
consent.intro: You are about to start the process of donating information about your Instagram use to our study. The data that we ask you to donate will be used for academic research to gain insight into social media use and wellbeing. Only counts are extracted: for each day, how many posts and videos you viewed, ads you saw or clicked, things you liked, commented on, saved or published, searches you made, accounts you followed, new followers, and messages you sent and received, plus the interest topics Instagram assigned to you. The content itself is never read or transmitted: no usernames or names of other people, no links, no message or comment text, no captions, photos or videos, no search terms, no locations, and no login or device information.
consent.process: We will walk you through this process step by step. During this process no data is stored or sent to a server. You can filter by date and delete rows from the data before donating. Data will only be donated and stored when you click the button "Yes, donate" on the page that shows your data.

sections.title: Who is running this study
paragraphs: This study is run by researchers at the University of Surrey: Dr Tamas Foldes (Surrey Sleep Research Centre), Dr Zsofia Zavecz and Dr Oscar Ferrante (School of Psychology). The University of Surrey is the data controller, which means it is responsible for your data.
For questions, or to withdraw your donation, email t.foldes@surrey.ac.uk.

sections.title: What we store
paragraphs: When you click "Yes, donate", we store:
items: the data you choose to donate on the review page, without any rows or data types you removed;
your submission ID (a random 16-digit number shown after you donate) and the date and time of your donation;

two technical details that your browser sends to every website: a scrambled code made from your IP address (the address itself is not stored), and your browser's identification string (its name, version and operating system). These are used only to block repeated or automated submissions.

sections.title: Storage, access and retention
paragraphs: We do not ask for your name or email address.
Your donation is encrypted as soon as it reaches our server and is stored on servers managed by the University of Surrey. Only the research team named above holds the key that can decrypt it.

Before your donation is sent, Cloudflare, a security service, checks that you are a person and not an automated program. Cloudflare receives your IP address for this check. It is not used for advertising or analytics.
Your data will be kept for 10 years after the study ends and then deleted.

sections.title: How your data is used and shared
paragraphs: Your donation is pseudonymised, not anonymous. It is not stored with your name or email address, but detailed records with exact times (for example the times of your activity on Instagram) could in principle be linked to you by someone who already knows a lot about you. For that reason:
items: the individual records you donate stay with the University of Surrey research team and are not published or shared with anyone else;
publications and presentations contain only aggregate results, such as averages across many participants, from which no individual can be identified.

sections.title: Your rights and how to withdraw
paragraphs: Taking part is voluntary. You can stop at any point before you click "Yes, donate", and nothing will be sent.

After donating, you can withdraw within 1 month: email t.foldes@surrey.ac.uk with your submission ID and we will delete your donation. Keep the ID safe. We do not know who you are, so the ID is the only way to find your donation. After 1 month your data may already be part of our analyses, and it can no longer be withdrawn.

The University of Surrey processes your data under UK data protection law (UK GDPR) as a task in the public interest (Article 6(1)(e)), with safeguards including encryption and pseudonymisation. Research ethics also requires your explicit consent, which is why we ask for it below.

The University's information governance page explains your data protection rights and how to contact its Data Protection Officer. You also have the right to complain to the Information Commissioner's Office (ico.org.uk).

agreementPoints: you explicitly and voluntarily agree to donate the data shown on the review page for this research.
you understand that your donation is pseudonymised, not anonymous, that the individual records stay with the research team, and that only aggregate results will be published.
you understand that you can withdraw your donation within 1 month by emailing your submission ID to t.foldes@surrey.ac.uk, and not after that.
consent.agreementCheckbox: I have read and agree with the above terms.

upload.title: Upload File
upload.intro: Please request a copy of your Instagram data: in the Instagram app go to your profile → menu (☰) → Accounts Center → Your information and permissions → Download your information → Download or transfer information. Choose your Instagram account, select "All available information" (or at least "Your activity", "Ads information" and "Connections"), choose "Download to device", set the date range to "All time", and importantly set Format to "JSON" (not HTML). Meta will notify you when the file is ready, usually within a day. Download the .zip file and upload it here without unpacking it. If your export came as several .zip files, upload the first one.
upload.processing: Processing your file... This may take a few moments for large exports.
upload.incorrectFile: The uploaded file might be incorrect, in HTML format, or void of Instagram activity.
upload.possibleIssues: We were unable to find any recognizable Instagram activity in the uploaded file. This could mean:
issuePoints: The export was made in HTML format instead of JSON (please request a new export and choose JSON)
The file is a Facebook export rather than an Instagram export
Your export was split into several .zip files and this part contains only media
The file is corrupted or incomplete
upload.checkFile: Please check that you have uploaded the Instagram export .zip in JSON format or contact the researchers for assistance.
upload.note: Note: The process to extract the correct data from the file is done on your own computer. No data is stored or sent yet. Extraction may take a while for large exports.

filter.intro: Determine whether you would like to donate the data below. Carefully check the data and adjust when required. You can filter by date range and delete rows. With your donation you contribute to the previously described research. Thank you in advance.
filter.donationPrompt: Do you want to donate the above data?
filter.note: Note: Sending the data may take several seconds depending on the data size.

thankyou.title: Thank You!
thankyou.successMessage: Your data has been successfully submitted. Thank you for your contribution!
thankyou.saveId: Please save this ID. We do not know who you are, so it is the only way to find your donation. To withdraw within 1 month of today, email this ID to t.foldes@surrey.ac.uk.
thankyou.deleteFile: For maximum security, please now delete the file you uploaded everywhere it is: on the phone or computer where you saved it, in any copy you used to move it (an email you sent yourself, a cloud drive, the Downloads folder), and in the trash or recycle bin.
thankyou.declineMessage: Thank you for your time. Your decision has been recorded and no data has been shared.
